user_query: We are designing a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a BCMA‑targeted antibody‑drug conjugate (ADC) in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients who have received 3 or more prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, lenalidomide, and an anti‑CD38 monoclonal antibody. The trial will enrol patients globally across North America, Europe, and Asia‑Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will submit to NICE and ICER for HTA. The ADC is given intravenously every 3 weeks. The manufacturer predicts peripheral neuropathy, fatigue, and corneal toxicity as key adverse events. Our TPP aims to demonstrate superiority in pain reduction, physical function, and overall HRQoL compared to standard of care. We also want to capture treatment tolerability and specific sensory neuropathy. Please generate a full COA strategy.
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** The trial requires a comprehensive PRO strategy emphasising disease‑specific pain and neuropathy capture using EORTC QLQ‑MY20 as the primary MM‑specific instrument alongside EORTC QLQ‑C30 for regulatory submission [TI-005].

**Key challenge:** EMA and FDA have rejected or limited PRO evidence to exploratory status for recent RRMM drugs due to open‑label bias, missing data, and lack of formal hypotheses [RR-013], [RR-014], [RR-015].

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ‑C30 + EORTC QLQ‑MY20 + EQ‑5D‑5L, mirroring A.R.R.O.W.'s successful 3‑instrument core battery that demonstrated significant change in Global Health Status and fatigue [TI-001], [TI-005], [TI-002].

**Critical gap:** No validated instruments for BCMA‑ADC corneal toxicity in multiple myeloma — PRO‑CTCAE and OSDI used in DREAMM‑7 showed substantial safety signal (55% severe blurred vision) but no formal efficacy labelling [CT-001].

## Key Observations

• DREAMM-7 showed substantial ocular toxicity (55% severe blurred vision) using PRO-CTCAE/OSDI but achieved no formal label claims, highlighting the regulatory challenge for BCMA-ADC tolerability endpoints [CT-001].

• A.R.R.O.W. demonstrated that EORTC QLQ-C30 can achieve formal FDA label claims in MM, specifically for Global Health Status improvement (p=0.0001), providing a validated regulatory pathway [CT-003].

• Three major CD38 antibody trials (MAIA, ALCYONE, ANDROMEDA) all demonstrated significant EQ-5D-5L improvements, establishing this as the mandatory HTA utility instrument for MM regulatory submissions [TI-002].

• EORTC QLQ-MY20 translation limitations (only 1 language in KG data) create operational risk for global trials despite strong MM-specific content validity and regulatory acceptance when paired with QLQ-C30 [TI-005].

• Recent EMA/FDA reviews rejected or limited PRO evidence to exploratory status due to open-label bias, missing data, and inadequate statistical planning, requiring enhanced methodological rigor [RR-013], [RR-014].

• MySIm-Q demonstrated superior MM symptom sensitivity (p=0.0003 for time to deterioration) but lacks broad translation availability and regulatory precedent compared to established EORTC instruments [TI-006].

## Comparator Analysis

DREAMM-7 and DREAMM-8 represent the most relevant comparators, both testing BCMA-directed ADCs in RRMM populations using EORTC QLQ-C30 as the core instrument. DREAMM-7 additionally used PRO-CTCAE and OSDI to capture ocular toxicity but demonstrated substantial safety signals (55% severe blurred vision) without achieving formal label claims [CT-001]. A.R.R.O.W. (carfilzomib, proteasome inhibitor class) successfully achieved a formal Global Health Status label claim using EORTC QLQ-C30 (p=0.0001) alongside EQ-5D-5L and EORTC QLQ-MY20 [CT-003]. If the current trial aims to show superiority in pain reduction and physical function, using EORTC QLQ-C30 — the same instrument that detected change in A.R.R.O.W. — would allow direct cross-trial comparison in regulatory submissions. This is a recognised regulatory strategy. The single instrument best supported by same-class comparators for pain and physical function domains is EORTC QLQ-C30, used successfully across both DREAMM trials.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument & Version | Preferred Value Set | Current Battery Status | Risk if Omitted |
|----------|-------------------------------|-------------------|----------------------|-----------------|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | England 5L value set | In candidates | QALY calculation impossible; NICE will issue a Request for Additional Data, delaying reimbursement by ≥12 months |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L | US value set | In candidates | Cost-effectiveness model cannot be constructed; ICER assessment limited to clinical effectiveness only, reducing formulary access likelihood |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to use EORTC QLQ-MY20 despite severe translation limitations (only 1 validated language in KG) given its MM-specific content validity and neuropathy coverage matching the TPP, versus relying solely on EORTC QLQ-C30 which has broader translation availability but less disease-specific sensitivity.

2. Whether to add FACT/GOG-NTX for dedicated neuropathy capture given ENDEAVOR showed sensitivity (p=0.0002) but translations require custom commissioning via FACITtrans, or rely on EORTC QLQ-MY20's neuropathy items which have weaker psychometric evidence but existing translations.

3. Assessment frequency strategy: adopt the DREAMM-7 Q3W schedule (matching IV administration) versus A.R.R.O.W.'s Q2-cycle schedule which achieved formal regulatory claims, considering patient burden and trial operational complexity.

4. Ocular toxicity capture: include PRO-CTCAE/OSDI mirroring DREAMM-7's approach despite no formal label claims achieved, or develop a streamlined symptom-specific module given the predicted corneal toxicity and substantial safety signals (55% severe blurred vision).

5. Primary versus secondary endpoint hierarchy: pre-specify Global Health Status as the key secondary PRO following A.R.R.O.W.'s successful regulatory strategy, versus pain response as primary given the TPP focus on pain reduction and the mixed results across BCMA-ADC comparators.
